items.question: How does the streaming variant of DeepWalk change the learning process when the entire graph is not known in advance, and what is one tradeoff of using this approach?
items.gold_answer: In the streaming variant of DeepWalk, small walks are passed directly to the representation learning code and the model is updated immediately, without needing knowledge of the full graph. Because a decaying learning rate is no longer possible, the learning rate must be initialized to a small constant value, which takes longer to learn but may still be worthwhile in some applications.
items.evidence_quote: In this variant small walks from the graph are passed directly to the representation learning code, and the model is updated directly.

items.question: Under what conditions can DeepWalk still build a Hierarchical Softmax tree in the streaming setting, and how are new vertices handled?
items.gold_answer: DeepWalk can still build a Hierarchical Softmax tree if the cardinality of V is known, or at least can be bounded. In that case, the tree can be built for the maximum value, and vertices can be assigned to one of the remaining leaves when they are first seen.
items.evidence_quote: If the cardinality of V is known (or can be bounded), we can build the Hierarchical Softmax tree for that maximum value.

items.question: Why might Huffman coding still be usable in the streaming version of DeepWalk, and what does it optimize?
items.gold_answer: If the model can estimate vertex frequency a priori, DeepWalk can still use Huffman coding in the streaming setting. The purpose is to decrease frequent element access times.

items.question: How are non-random walks used in DeepWalk-style modeling, and what additional type of information do they capture compared with ordinary graph structure?
items.gold_answer: In the non-random-walk setting, graphs generated by agents interacting with sequences of elements are used to feed the modeling phase directly. This captures not only network structure but also the frequency with which paths are traversed, and the same idea can be applied to language modeling by treating sentences as purposive walks in a language network.
items.evidence_quote: Graphs sampled in this way will not only capture information related to network structure, but also to the frequency at which paths are traversed.
